title: Compare and Order Integers and Rational Numbers
objective: I can compare and order integers using a number line.
model: horizontal number line: farther left is less, farther right is greater; the open side of < or > faces the greater number

widgets.root: Review of 7-3 only (absolute value), which is the contrast the lesson needs (|−10| > |−2| but −10 < −2); keys 9, 7, 0 checked.

widgets.component: true statement among four, least of −3,5,−8,2,0, |−8|; error '−5 > −2 because 5 > 2'
widgets.root: Keys −5 < −2, −8 and 8 verified; the error flags the student's reasoning step (e=1), which is the first wrong step.

widgets.component: compare five pairs with < > =, warmest of −12, −5, 3 °F, order −8 and −15
generated: true statement, least/greatest, order a list, symbol choice, incl. fractions and decimals at L3
widgets.root: Spot-checked 5 seeds per level: every key right, including mixed values such as −2 1/5 > −2.5 and 8/5 > 1 1/2. L3 widens from integers to the rational numbers 7-2 already placed on the line; the key idea names rational numbers even though the objective line says integers.

widgets.where: Practice 4.7; Challenge 3.1-3.2 (act:nline mode order L2, L3, L4)
widgets.component: tap numbers into the line in order; each drops onto its position
widgets.root: Real model: items land at their true positions, 2+ negatives per set, wrong orders are named ('ignored-sign', 'reversed'); labels use U+2212; the line is 0.5/0.25 step with integer labels.

widgets.component: coldest day, colder of −4 °F and −1 °F, order the temperatures coldest to warmest
widgets.root: These are Connect checks stripped of config connect.scenario (the weather-station list Monday −4, Tuesday 2, Wednesday −7, Thursday −1, Friday 5). 5.1 names four days and 5.3 lists five numbers (including 5) with no list on the page, and the correct 5.3 choice is simply the only ascending one, so it can be picked without reading the data or ordering anything.
widgets.replacement: Put the data on the page: stem 'Monday −4 °F, Tuesday 2 °F, Wednesday −7 °F, Thursday −1 °F, Friday 5 °F' with viz {t:'nline', min:-8, max:6, step:1, marks:[...five days...]}. Make 5.3 an act:nline {mode:'order'} item over those five values (the student builds the ascending list instead of choosing it) and keep 5.1 as 'which day was coldest' with day-name choices. Keep 5.2 as is.

widgets.component: ascending list of integers, symbol for −8 ___ −5, greatest integer less than −4
widgets.root: Keys (−5,−2,0,3,7), '<' and −5 verified; '≥' is a plausible-but-false distractor.

widgets.component: generated least/greatest, true statement, 'which city was warmest' with reasons
widgets.root: L4 reason-choices (−16 > −19 because −19 is farther left) and temperature-ranking contexts checked over 5 seeds.

widgets.component: error '−8 > −3'; write the −100 vs 1 and −100 vs −1 argument; rank four rooms with 'warmer than it' counts; five clues on a drawn line; count scores > −3; ledger balances
widgets.root: Table recomputed (freezer rank 1/3 warmer, attic 4/0, cellar 2/2, study 3/1); line order E, A, B, C, D matches the drawn marks −12, −9, −4, 0, 3; counts 3 and ledger order $8, −$12, −$30, −$45 right.

widgets.component: true/false sort of six comparisons; three error analyses (ignore signs, symbol direction, 0 as least); Ximena/Yuri/Zoe; ordering; decimals; integers between −4 and 3; temperature range
widgets.root: Sort bins and error steps (e=0, 2, 0) verified; 6 integers between −4 and 3 and a range of 13 °C are right; the drawn line puts P, Q, R at −7, −2, 4.

typography: Practice 1.1-1.3, 2.1-2.4, 3.1 (table), 3.2, 3.3, 5.4 and Challenge 2.1, 2.2 print negatives with an ASCII hyphen-minus (-5 < -2, -12°F, 'Compare -3 and -8'); 2.3, 5.1-5.3, 5.5 and every generated item use U+2212.
